findings.problem: status is a free-form String, allowing any invalid value (e.g. "cancelled", "", "SENT") while the domain only expects a bounded set of lifecycle states.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream logic checking status == "sent" cannot be exhaustive; typos or unexpected strings silently bypass guards.
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with an enum `PacketStatus { Pending, Sent }` and store `status: PacketStatus`.

findings.problem: is_validated (bool) and is_sent (bool) are independent flags from status (String), creating logically impossible states such as status="sent" with is_sent=false, or status="pending" with is_sent=true.
findings.failure_mode: State-machine invariants are not enforced at the type level; callers can construct or mutate PacketWorkflow into inconsistent states that break downstream assumptions.
findings.fix: Replace `status: String`, `is_validated: bool`, and `is_sent: bool` with a single typestate enum `PacketState { New, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }` and make invalid transitions unconstructable.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes `mut item: PacketWorkflow` and mutates fields in-place (item.status, item.is_sent), violating the functional-core principle of pure, non-mutating transformations.
findings.failure_mode: Callers lose immutability guarantees; the function has observable side effects on the input value, making it harder to reason about and test.
findings.fix: Change signature to `pub fn mark_sent(item: PacketWorkflow) -> PacketWorkflow` and return a newly constructed PacketWorkflow instead of mutating the input.

findings.problem: item.status = "sent".to_string() performs a heap allocation every time mark_sent is called, even though the struct already owns a String. This is wasteful and allocates unboundedly.
findings.failure_mode: Under high throughput, repeated allocations of the same constant string waste heap memory and increase GC pressure without purpose.
findings.fix: Replace with direct enum variant construction (once `status` is an enum), or use `item.status = "sent".into()` if keeping String, or better yet drop the String entirely in favor of the enum.

findings.problem: PacketWorkflow fields are raw primitives (String, bool, Option<u64>) with no validation at construction. There is no constructor enforcing that fields are consistent (e.g. sent_at_epoch_ms present only when sent).
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct PacketWorkflow with mismatched fields, e.g. is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None, bypassing all invariants at compile time.
findings.fix: Provide a fallible constructor `PacketWorkflow::new(...)` or build via typed constructors per state variant that guarantees field consistency by construction.

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for mark_sent or any hot-path through PacketWorkflow. Allocation behaviour of .to_string() is unmeasured.
findings.failure_mode: Performance claims about mark_sent are unverified; hidden allocations may become a bottleneck under load.
findings.fix: Add a Criterion or similar benchmark for mark_sent to measure allocation frequency and throughput before and after the enum/typestate fix.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent throughput or allocation profile
no profiler data for hot-path execution
no second-ring analysis of the state-transition graph
residual_risk: static review only with no commands run; the crate represents illegal states at the type level, has no exhaustive domain enum for status, uses mutable in-place mutation, and lacks benchmarks or profiler evidence. A typestate/enum refactor of PacketWorkflow and a pure mark_sent are required before this crate meets Holzman Rust standards.
